newsitem.title: USA: Grand Union debt continues decline.
newsitem.headline: Grand Union debt continues decline.

text.p: Grand Union Co debt fell 1-1/2 points on Monday, in a continuation of volatile trading from last week, high-yield traders said.
"Trading continues to be volatile in Grand Union paper," said one high-yield trader. "The 12 percent notes traded as high as 80 bid at the open but later came off to trade at 77-1/2 bid."
Grand Union debt fell from the high eighties last Thursday after dissappointing earnings and news hit the market of a corporate restructruring, leading to 80 layoffs, players said.

The company reported 1997 fourth quarter losses of $78.1 million versus losses of $29.3 million a year ago. Its fiscal 1997 year-end loss was $185.4 million versus an operating loss of $139.2 million in 1996.
After the news Moody's Investors Service Inc and Standard & Poor's cut the supermarket operator's debt ratings.
Grand Union operates 226 retail food stores in six Northeastern states.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1675 ))
